{{Short description|1=Family of algebraic curves of the form r = sec(θ) + a*cos(θ)}}
[[Image:Conchoid of deSluze.svg|right|thumb|300px|The Conchoid of de Sluze for several values of {{mvar|a}}]]

In [[algebraic geometry]], the '''conchoids of de Sluze''' are a [[family of curves|family]] of [[plane curve]]s studied in 1662 by Walloon mathematician [[René François Walter]], baron de Sluze.<ref>{{citation|title=History of Mathematics, Volume 2|first=David Eugene|last=Smith|publisher=Courier Dover Publications|year=1958|isbn=9780486204307|page=327|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uTytJGnTf1kC&pg=PA327}}.</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://core.ac.uk/download/pdf/82380781.pdf |title=Conchoid of de Sluze by J. Dziok et al.on Computers and Mathematics with Applications 61 (2011) 2605–2613}}</ref>

The curves are defined by the [[polar coordinates|polar]] equation
:<math>r=\sec\theta+a\cos\theta \,.</math>
In [[Cartesian coordinate system|cartesian coordinates]], the curves satisfy the [[implicit function|implicit equation]]
:<math>(x-1)(x^2+y^2)=ax^2 \,</math>
except that for {{math|1=''a'' = 0}} the implicit form has an [[acnode]] {{math|(0,0)}} not present in polar form.

They are [[rational curve|rational]], [[circular algebraic curve|circular]], [[cubic plane curve]]s.

These expressions have an [[asymptote]] {{math|1=''x'' = 1}} (for {{math|''a'' &ne; 0}}). The point most distant from the asymptote is {{math|(1 + ''a'', 0)}}. {{math|(0,0)}} is a [[crunode]] for {{math|''a'' < &minus;1}}.

The area between the curve and the [[asymptote]] is, for {{math|''a'' &ge; &minus;1}},
:<math>|a|(1+a/4)\pi \,</math> 
while for {{math|''a'' < &minus;1}}, the area is
:<math>\left(1-\frac a2\right)\sqrt{-(a+1)}-a\left(2+\frac a2\right)\arcsin\frac1{\sqrt{-a}}.</math> 
If {{math|''a'' < &minus;1}}, the curve will have a loop. The area of the loop is
:<math>\left(2+\frac a2\right)a\arccos\frac1{\sqrt{-a}} + \left(1-\frac a2\right)\sqrt{-(a+1)}.</math>

Four of the family have names of their own:
*{{math|1=''a'' = 0}}, [[line (mathematics)|line]] (asymptote to the rest of the family)
*{{math|1=''a'' = &minus;1}}, [[cissoid of Diocles]] 
*{{math|1=''a'' = &minus;2}}, [[strophoid|right strophoid]]
*{{math|1=''a'' = &minus;4}}, [[trisectrix of Maclaurin]]
